Automatic arrival records

Your first observed arrival, on your computer.

Understand which login and unlock events create an arrival, and when to correct it manually.

Mac 1.5.15 build31 · Windows 1.5.13
OverviewHow to useExampleScope and limitsRelated features

What creates an arrival

Mac records the first valid observed login-item launch or screen unlock while running. Windows uses an actual SessionUnlock event observed while the app runs. Starting Windows automatically at login is not itself an arrival event.

Later unlocks preserve today’s existing arrival, manual edits and day-off choice. Attendance works without an account and stays separately on each computer.

Use automatic recording

  1. Install and run the app, then set your work and break hours.
  2. Enable login startup if needed. Mac attempts registration on first launch; Windows requires you to enable it in settings.
  3. Check today’s arrival after the first valid observed login or unlock.
  4. Enter a manual arrival if you had already started or the app recorded an unlock at home.

Automatic detection starts at 06:00 local time. Regular or afternoon-off observations from 06:00 through 07:59:59 become 08:00 on the same day. Earlier observations are ignored. Morning off keeps its 13:00–15:00 window.

An early-morning example

A first valid unlock at 06:30 on a regular workday becomes an 08:00 arrival. Eight work hours plus one break hour gives a 17:00 expected departure. This example assumes no last-Friday or other reduction.

Unlocking again at 09:10 preserves the 08:00 record. An event at 06:30 while the app was closed cannot be reconstructed later.

Scope and limits

Ordinary manual launch, wake and session activation alone do not create an arrival. The app does not detect office location or Wi-Fi, so an unlock at home may count.

Take today off clears today’s arrival after confirmation and pauses automatic recording. Saving a manual arrival resumes it. Mac’s leave choice is separate and retains the existing arrival.

The app does not detect and record actual departure. Expected departure is calculated personal guidance, not official attendance or payroll evidence. Mac and Windows records do not sync.
